Fairness of a lineup from mock witnesses

Source: R/lnroc.R
lnsize.Rd

Asks whether a lineup singles out its suspect. People who never saw the crime (mock witnesses) read the witness's description and pick the lineup member who fits it best; in a fair lineup of k they pick each member about equally often. A choice of 0 records a mock witness who chose no one. With n mock witnesses, m of whom chose a member, and o_i the choices of member i:

Usage

lnsize(choice, k = NULL, susp = 1, level = 0.95)

Arguments

choice

The lineup position each mock witness picked: whole numbers from 0, 0 for a mock witness who chose no one; one member at least must be chosen.

k

NULL for the largest position picked, or the lineup's size: one whole number from 2 to 67108864 (2^26).

susp

The suspect's position: one whole number from 1 to k.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class lnsize, a list: count, the choices of each position; stat, a named vector (n, k, nm (the mock witnesses who chose a member), psusp, pbin, fsize, esize, esizeb, etr, etrlo, etrhi); and susp.

Details

  • psusp, the share of the n who picked the suspect, and pbin, the binomial chance of that many or more among the m if each member were picked with chance 1 / k (a small pbin is bias against the suspect);

  • fsize, the functional size of Wells, Leippe and Ostrom (1979), n over the number who picked the suspect (k for a fair lineup);

  • esize, the effective size of Malpass (1981), ka - sum |o_i - ea| / (2 ea): the members nobody chose (null foils) are left out, ka is the number of members chosen at least once, ea = m / ka, and the sum runs over those ka members; it reduces the size by how far members are chosen below chance. esizeb is the same without the adjustment (k and e = m / k, the sum over all members), the form Tredoux (1996, Chapter 6, equation 5; 1999, p. S13) prefers because a member can go unchosen by chance;

  • etr, the effective size E' = 1 / (1 - I) = 1 / sum p_i^2 of Tredoux (1998), p_i = o_i / m, with its interval: the large-sample interval of I = 1 - sum p_i^2, whose variance is 4 (sum p^3 - (sum p^2)^2) / m (Agresti and Agresti 1978), with both ends taken to 1 / (1 - I) (Tredoux 1996, Chapter 6, equations 8, 9 and 11). etrhi is Inf when the upper end of I reaches 1.

The tests reproduce Tables 4.1 (p. 67), 4.2 (p. 70) and 6.6 (p. 144) of Tredoux (1996) and Table 1 (p. S10) of Tredoux (1999). Two printed values there do not follow from their own counts and formulas: lineup i of Table 4.2 (1, 0, 12, 12, 0, 11) has an adjusted effective size of 3.11, printed 3.17 (the unadjusted value), and the lower end of E' in Table 6.6 is 1 / (1 - 0.7015) = 3.350, printed 3.503.

References

Malpass, R. S. (1981). Effective size and defendant bias in eyewitness identification lineups. Law and Human Behavior, 5(4), 299-309. doi:10.1007/BF01044945

Tredoux, C. G. (1996). Evaluating the Fairness of Identification Parades with Measures of Facial Similarity. PhD thesis, University of Cape Town.

Tredoux, C. G. (1998). Statistical inference on measures of lineup fairness. Law and Human Behavior, 22(2), 217-237. doi:10.1023/A:1025746220886

Tredoux, C. (1999). Statistical considerations when determining measures of lineup size and lineup bias. Applied Cognitive Psychology, 13(S1), S9-S26. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1099-0720(199911)13:1+<S9::AID-ACP634>3.0.CO;2-1

Agresti, A. and Agresti, B. F. (1978). Statistical analysis of qualitative variation. Sociological Methodology, 9, 204-237. doi:10.2307/270810

Wells, G. L., Leippe, M. R. and Ostrom, T. M. (1979). Guidelines for empirically assessing the fairness of a lineup. Law and Human Behavior, 3(4), 285-293. doi:10.1007/BF01039807

Examples

# 40 mock witnesses, a lineup of six, the suspect in position 3
ch <- c(rep(3, 15), rep(1, 5), rep(2, 6), rep(4, 4), rep(5, 7), rep(6, 3))
lnsize(ch, k = 6, susp = 3)
#> lnsize: 40 mock witnesses, lineup of 6, suspect in position 3
#>            n            k           nm        psusp         pbin        fsize 
#> 40.000000000  6.000000000 40.000000000  0.375000000  0.001282306  2.666666667 
#>        esize       esizeb          etr        etrlo        etrhi 
#>  4.700000000  4.700000000  4.444444444  3.345535088  6.618389805
